Can You Buy a Home in South Carolina With a Reverse Mortgage?

By Paul Hankins, Founder, CEO and Broker, NMLS #281393BrickWood Mortgage, Surfside Beach, SC

The short answer

Yes. If you are 62 or older, a HECM for Purchase lets you buy your next home with one closing and no monthly mortgage payment. You bring a large down payment, often from selling your current home, and the reverse mortgage pays the rest. You must move in within 60 days and keep paying taxes, insurance and upkeep.

  • Age 62+The youngest borrower, at closing
  • 60 daysTo move in after closing
  • One closingThe purchase and the reverse mortgage together
  • $1,249,125The 2026 HECM limit on home value used

How a HECM for Purchase works

A HECM (Home Equity Conversion Mortgage) is the reverse mortgage insured by the Federal Housing Administration (FHA). Most people use one on a home they already own. A HECM for Purchase uses it to buy a new home instead.

Here is the idea in plain terms. The reverse mortgage pays part of the price at closing. You pay the rest from your own money. After closing, you own the home and make no monthly mortgage payment. The loan balance grows over time and is repaid when you sell, move out for good, or after the last borrower dies, usually from the sale of the home.

How much you bring to closing

You pay the difference between the price and the amount the reverse mortgage can lend, plus any loan costs you do not finance, minus your earnest money. The amount the loan can lend is called the principal limit.

The principal limit depends on three things:

  • the age of the youngest borrower, or of an eligible non-borrowing spouse; the older you are, the more the loan can lend;
  • current interest rates;
  • the home's price or appraised value, whichever is lower, up to $1,249,125 for 2026 case numbers.

Because the share changes with age and rates, we give you the exact figure in writing for your age and price, not a rule of thumb.

An example, in words

A retired couple sells their home in Ohio and finds a house near Murrells Inlet. At their ages, the reverse mortgage can lend part of the price. They pay the rest from the sale of the Ohio house, close once, and move in the next week. They keep the rest of their savings, and they make no monthly mortgage payment. They still pay the property tax, the insurance and the HOA.

The rules you must meet

  • Age. The youngest borrower must be 62 or older at closing.
  • Counseling. You meet with a HUD-approved counselor before you apply. The counselor is independent of us and explains the loan, its costs and other choices.
  • Your own money. The down payment comes from cash you have or from selling your assets, such as your current home. Money from the seller cannot be used for it.
  • Moving in. Every borrower must make the home their principal residence within 60 days of closing.
  • A financial check. We confirm you can keep up with taxes, insurance and upkeep. The lender may set some money aside for those bills if needed.
  • An existing reverse mortgage. If you have one on your current home, it must be paid off before the new one closes.

The seller may pay only the fees a seller must pay by law, the fees sellers customarily pay locally, and a home warranty. A seller cannot pay your other loan costs or give you a credit toward the price.

Which homes qualify

The home must be finished and ready to live in, with a certificate of occupancy for a new build. Serious safety or soundness problems must be repaired by the seller before closing.

A condo qualifies only if the building is acceptable to HUD under FHA's condo rules. Not every condo building is FHA-approved, so we check the building before you make an offer. Our guide to condo mortgage requirements explains what buildings must pass.

What you still pay after closing

No monthly mortgage payment is required. You still pay:

  • property taxes;
  • homeowners insurance, and flood insurance if the home is in a flood zone (see flood insurance and your mortgage);
  • HOA dues, if any;
  • repairs and upkeep.

Falling behind on these can make the loan come due. Interest and the FHA mortgage insurance premium are added to the loan balance each month, so the balance grows and the equity left for you or your heirs shrinks over time. You may make payments if you choose. To understand what happens later, read who is responsible for a reverse mortgage after death.

HECM for Purchase compared with paying cash

Pay cashHECM for Purchase
Cash needed at closingThe full pricePart of the price, plus unfinanced costs
Monthly mortgage paymentNoneNone required
Savings left after the moveLessMore
Loan costsNoneFHA insurance premium, interest and closing costs
Equity in the home laterAll of itLess, as the balance grows

A HECM for Purchase suits a buyer who wants to keep savings for health care, travel or family, and plans to stay in the home for years. It suits less well a buyer who may move again soon, because the loan costs come early.

The steps, from offer to move-in

  1. Estimate. We give you the amount you would bring at your age and price range.
  2. Counseling. You complete a session with a HUD-approved counselor.
  3. Offer. You make an offer, with the reverse mortgage named as your financing.
  4. Application and appraisal. We take your application, order the FHA appraisal and complete the financial check.
  5. Closing. You bring your share, sign once, and get the keys.
  6. Move in. Within 60 days.

For how a HECM compares with borrowing against a home you already own, see reverse mortgage vs home equity loan and our reverse mortgage loans page.

HECM for Purchase questions

How much down payment do you need for a reverse mortgage purchase?

You pay the difference between the price and the amount the HECM can lend, plus any loan costs you do not finance. The amount the HECM can lend rises with the age of the youngest borrower and changes with interest rates, so it is figured for each buyer.

Can the seller pay closing costs on a HECM for Purchase?

Only in part. The seller may pay fees a seller must pay by law, fees sellers customarily pay locally, and a home warranty. Other loan costs and any credit toward the price must come from you or the loan.

How soon must I move in after a HECM for Purchase?

Every borrower must make the home their principal residence within 60 days of closing.

Can I use a HECM for Purchase to buy a condo?

Yes, if the condo building is acceptable to HUD under FHA's condo rules. We check the building's status before you make an offer.

Do I make monthly payments on a reverse mortgage used to buy a home?

No monthly mortgage payment is required. You must still pay property taxes, homeowners insurance, any flood insurance and HOA dues, and keep the home repaired. You may make payments on the loan if you choose.

What is the HECM limit for 2026?

For FHA case numbers assigned in 2026, the HECM maximum claim amount is $1,249,125 in every area. A home can cost more, but the loan is figured on value up to that limit.
